**Resubmitted — status unchanged: compliant.**

The verifier's single failed check was `Customer convenience termination present`, and its own notes confirm this is a phrasing artifact rather than a substantive gap. I repaired the finding by reconciling that artifact explicitly on the record rather than by changing the classification:

- **Why the regex missed it:** Section 14 grants the right functionally — "election to terminate this Agreement," with no cause, consent, or justification requirement — without ever using the word "convenience." I verified the only occurrence of "convenience" in the document is the captions boilerplate at §22 (p0088). The rule's actual test is *who may terminate without cause, on what notice, at what cost*, and §14 answers all three in our favour.
- **What I added:** the keyword-artifact reconciliation, an explicit four-point walkthrough of the material terms (notice ~30–60 days; no fee; no Vendor mid-term exit; 1-year term so the multi-year walk-away trigger is inapplicable), and p0043 to the cited paragraphs so the "Subject to Section 4" blank is traceable in the record.

**No redline was proposed**, which is the required output here — the clause meets the preferred position, and the playbook is explicit that a compliant clause is not redlined.

One judgment call worth surfacing: I considered adding "for convenience" to §14 to satisfy the keyword check directly, but declined and instead logged it as an optional, only-if-already-reopened drafting note. Editing a clause that already sits at preferred purely to match a search pattern would mean reopening a favourable provision for cosmetic gain — the downside risk outweighs the benefit.

Carried forward for negotiation follow-up (not deviations): §13's mis-cross-reference to "Section 12" for termination, and the unfilled `____ months` Support Services commitment at p0043, which should be set at a figure we're comfortable with so it can't be argued to qualify our §14 exit.
